text: We evaluated a two-phase curriculum that trains first on confident weak-labeled examples and then on the full weak-labeled set, with the second phase learning rate scaled by 0.1, on the BoolQ testbed. Across 3 seeds, the method reached a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.62. This is a single-setting measurement with a small number of seeds, and no baseline PGR was provided for comparison, so the number should be read as a standalone observation rather than evidence that the curriculum outperforms standard weak-to-strong training. No variance or standard error figures accompany the reported PGR, which further limits what can be inferred about run-to-run stability; with only 3 seeds, the spread could be substantial. Interpreting this result would require a matched baseline trained on the same data, dispersion estimates, and ideally additional testbeds, since BoolQ alone may not generalize. We therefore report the 0.62 PGR descriptively and treat the curriculum's benefit as untested.
